rules.name: Naming Consistency
checks: A new identifier follows the casing already used in the same module: snake_case for functions, variables and modules, PascalCase for classes, UPPER_CASE for module-level constants; no second style is introduced next to an existing one.
A name says what the value is or what the function does; an abbreviation is used only if the same module already uses it.
A repository, port or use case is named the way its siblings in the same layer are named (same suffix, same verb form).
A renamed symbol is renamed at every use inside the diff; no stale name remains in docstrings, tests or exports.

rules.name: Error Handling Standards
checks: Every external call and I/O operation (HTTP client, database, queue, file system, subprocess) has error handling on the path that needs it: a specific exception is caught or the failure is propagated deliberately.
No bare except and no except Exception that swallows the error; an error is handled, logged with context, or re-raised.
No empty except block and no except that only logs and continues where the caller expects a result.
A router does not catch exceptions to hide a failure; it decodes the transport contract, calls a use case and maps known domain errors to HTTP status codes.

rules.name: Complex Function Improvement Suggestions
checks: A function longer than 50 lines or nested more than 3 levels deep is split; name the piece that can be extracted.
A function with more than 5 parameters, or a boolean parameter that switches behaviour, takes a dataclass or Pydantic model, or becomes two functions.
Nested conditionals are replaced by guard clauses; a repeated if/elif cascade on the same discriminator is replaced by a mapping or polymorphism.
Business logic that appears in a router or an infrastructure adapter is moved into a use case or a domain service.

rules.name: Meaningful Comments for Complex Logic
checks: Non-obvious logic (a regex, a magic number, a workaround, an ordering constraint, a noqa or type: ignore) has a comment that says why, not what.
A comment or docstring that restates the code, or no longer matches the changed code next to it, is removed or updated.
A TODO or FIXME names an issue number or an owner.

rules.name: Test Coverage for Complex Functions
checks: New or changed logic with branches has a corresponding change in tests/test_<feature>.py in the same diff.

The change to a use case is accompanied by tests that fake its ports (Protocols) instead of real infrastructure; a change that needs a database is accompanied by tests marked integration that skip when TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset.
The change to an app file is accompanied by tests that cover its failure path (raised domain error, empty result, rejected input), not only the happy path.
Tests assert literal values taken from the spec, never values derived from the implementation under test.

rules.name: Clean Architecture Boundaries
checks: Dependency rule: entrypoints -> application -> domain, and infrastructure -> application/domain; a domain or application module never imports from infrastructure or entrypoints.
A port (interface) lives in the module that consumes it, not in the module that implements it.
Inside a UnitOfWork a repository calls flush, never commit; the use case commits.
No database transaction spans an LLM or GitHub call; network calls happen outside the transaction boundary.
New module code lands in app/modules/<m>/{domain,application,infrastructure} or app/common/, and a router in app/entrypoints/ contains no business logic.
